hypothesis: A minimal ISA v0 core (fetch/decode/execute, 4 registers, GPIO bus on uio[7:0], WAIT/branch/DECJNZ) can be implemented and differentially verified against an independent Python model within the Tiny Tapeout cmos5l template.
baseline: No RTL existed; repository contained only planning documents.
change: Added src/{project,core,alu,gpio,program_rom}.v, tools/{assembler,isa_model}.py, firmware/loop_demo.asm, test/test.py (differential cocotb test). Toolchain: Miniforge/conda-forge (iverilog 13.0, verilator 5.052, yosys 0.69, cocotb 2.0.1) installed without sudo.
result: Two bugs found and fixed during bring-up: (1) markdown-style backticks and a literal "*/" substring inside Verilog block comments caused Icarus preprocessor/parser errors (backticks are macro-expanded even inside comments; "GDIR*/GWR*" prematurely closed a block comment) - fixed by removing backticks/'*/' from all RTL comments. (2) A genuine RTL bug: `rd_val`/`rs_val` were continuous assignments driven by a function (`reg_read`) that read module-level regs (r0-r3) not in its argument list; Icarus only tracked the explicit argument (rd_idx) for re-evaluation, so back-to-back instructions targeting the same register (ANDI R0 -> ORI R0 -> XORI R0) read a stale value. Fixed by replacing the function call with explicit continuous-assign muxes. Also fixed a cocotb testbench issue (not an RTL bug): reading DUT-internal registers immediately after `await RisingEdge` raced with the DUT's own NBA updates; fixed with `await ReadOnly()` after each RisingEdge before sampling.
tests: test/test.py::test_isa_v0_differential (cocotb, Icarus Verilog): assembles firmware/loop_demo.asm, runs it on both RTL and tools/isa_model.py, asserts pc/r0-r3/z/halted/uio_oe/uio_out match every cycle.
outcome: PASS - 50 cycles, RTL matches Python model exactly, program reaches HALT.

hypothesis: The chip can be made genuinely reprogrammable after fabrication by adding a serial bootloader FSM (over the existing uio bus, no new pins) that writes a real program RAM, replacing the $readmemh-fixed ROM; ISA v1 also needs SHIFTOUT/SHIFTIN for byte-oriented firmware.
baseline: ISA v0: src/program_rom.v ($readmemh, fixed at elaboration), 19 opcodes, no shift instructions.
change: Added src/program_ram.v (writable), a bootloader FSM in src/core.v (LD_WAIT/LD_COUNT/LD_WORD/LD_DONE states) driven over uio[0:2] (LOAD_REQ/LOAD_CLK/LOAD_DATA), SHIFTOUT/SHIFTIN opcodes (19,20), test/bootload.py (cocotb driver for the protocol), and migrated the existing differential test off $readmemh entirely onto the bootloader path.
result: Two timing bugs found and fixed during bring-up: (1) the GPIO input synchronizer resets to 0 and takes 2 cycles to reflect the real external pin value, so sampling LOAD_REQ on the very first post-reset cycle always read 0 regardless of what the host drove - fixed with an explicit 2-cycle settle counter before the bootloader's first sample. (2) the cocotb bootloader driver hands off to normal execution mid-way through its final bit-clock pulse (the FSM transitions to LD_DONE partway through the driver's own trailing awaits), so a naive test setup assuming PC=0 immediately after the driver returns was wrong (observed PC=4 instead of the expected 1); fixed by snapshotting the RTL's actual post-load architectural state (pc/r0-r3/z/halted/wait_remaining/gpio_dir/gpio_out) into the Python model instead of assuming a fixed handoff cycle count.
tests: test/test.py::test_isa_v1_differential (cocotb, Icarus Verilog): loads firmware/loop_demo.asm (now exercising SHIFTOUT/SHIFTIN too) purely via test/bootload.py's serial protocol (no $readmemh anywhere), then differentially compares RTL against tools/isa_model.py every cycle.
outcome: PASS - 63 cycles, RTL matches Python model exactly, program reaches HALT, loaded entirely through the new bootloader mechanism.
